1.desc: Unspecified reason. Catch-all used when no specific reason applies; broadly honored by most supplicants.

2.desc: Previous authentication is no longer valid. Client's prior auth state is rejected; forces re-auth.

3.desc: Deauthenticated because sending STA is leaving the BSS. Classic 'go away'; most drivers tear down immediately.

4.desc: Deauthenticated due to inactivity. Clients often treat this as benign and reconnect quietly.

5.desc: Deauthenticated because AP is unable to handle all currently associated STAs. Triggers load-shedding logic.

6.desc: Class 2 frame received from nonauthenticated STA. Forces the client back to the authentication phase.

7.desc: Class 3 frame received from nonassociated STA. Forces full reassociation, not just reauth — most disruptive common code.

8.desc: Deauthenticated because sending STA is leaving the BSS. Natural deauth reason; fast path through supplicant state machine.

9.desc: STA requesting (re)association is not authenticated with responding STA. Forces reauth before reassoc.

10.desc: Deauthenticated because the information in the Power Capability element is unacceptable.

11.desc: Deauthenticated because the information in the Supported Channels element is unacceptable.

13.desc: Invalid information element. Malformed or unexpected IE in the association request.

14.desc: Message integrity code (MIC) failure. Security-relevant; some clients flush key state on this.

15.desc: 4-Way Handshake timeout. Clients often flush PMKSA state, not just association state.

16.desc: Group Key Handshake timeout. Re-keying failure; disrupts group-addressed traffic state.

17.desc: Information element in 4-Way Handshake different from (Re)Association Request/Probe Response/Beacon.

18.desc: Invalid group cipher. Security negotiation failure.

19.desc: Invalid pairwise cipher. Security negotiation failure.

21.desc: Unsupported RSNE version. Client's RSN capabilities not acceptable to the AP.

22.desc: Invalid RSNE contents. Malformed security element.

23.desc: IEEE 802.1X authentication failed. Supplicant typically retries the full EAP exchange.

24.desc: Cipher suite rejected because of the security policy. Policy mismatch.

25.desc: TDLS direct-link teardown. Only affects tunneled direct-link peers, not the main BSS link.

26.desc: TDLS peer is unreachable. TDLS-only; main link unaffected.

27.desc: TDLS peer has been torn down; AP does not permit TDLS. TDLS-only.

28.desc: TDLS peer cannot operate on the requested channel. TDLS-only.

29.desc: TDLS peer is not present. TDLS-only.

30.desc: AP does not allow TDLS. TDLS-only.

31.desc: AP does not support TDLS. TDLS-only.

32.desc: TDLS peer cannot operate on the requested channel. TDLS-only.

33.desc: TDLS peer does not support coexistence with the AP. TDLS-only.

34.desc: Deauthenticated because AP is unable to handle all currently associated STAs. Triggers load-shed logic; some clients back off reconnecting.

35.desc: Mesh STA is leaving the mesh. Mesh-only.

40.desc: Mesh STA closed the mesh. Mesh-only.

41.desc: Mesh STA reached maximum number of peerings. Mesh-only.

43.desc: Mesh STA does not support the requested channel. Mesh-only.

44.desc: Mesh peering rejected by the peer. Mesh-only.

45.desc: Authentication is not valid. Broad re-auth forcing.

47.desc: Authentication is not valid (alternate). Forcing reauth.
